items.title: Frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pairs and their real-field encoding
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary formulation prerequisite for the vector PEC scattering theorem (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $\omega>0$, let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set, and let $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ be the vacuum constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Phasor encoding] For every pair of $C^\infty$ maps $\widetilde E,\widetilde B:D\to\mathbb C^3$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) define the **associated real fields** $$E(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t}\bigr),\qquad B(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\widetilde B(x)e^{-i\omega t}\bigr)\qquad((x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R),$$ componentwise, with the complex exponential and real part of [[def-complex-exponential]] and [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]; this is the encoding convention of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] specialized from plane-wave amplitudes to a general $C^\infty$ amplitude, and the complex fields are not themselves physical fields. (b) [Source-free class] The pair $(\widetilde E,\widetilde B)$ is called a **frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on $D$** when it is $C^\infty$ and satisfies, on $D$, $$\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}\widetilde B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B,\qquad \operatorname{curl}\widetilde B=-i\omega\varepsilon_0\mu_0\widetilde E=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E,$$ with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] applied componentwise to the complex fields. The word 'source-free' records that the displayed equations carry no charge or current term; the associated real fields are read as an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]], $\omega$ is the angular frequency and $T:=2\pi/\omega$ the period. (c) [Status and scope] This item fixes the encoding, the four phasor equations and the terminology only. It asserts no equation for the associated real fields, no outgoing or boundary condition, no existence or uniqueness statement, no energy or flux reading and no empirical content. In particular the deduction that the associated real fields satisfy the smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations with zero sources is not part of this definition; for the pairs used on this page it is established by the exterior-scattering theorem recorded later on this page. Only $C^\infty$ pairs on an open set are defined, so no boundary trace, weak or distributional class is introduced here.
items.strategy: This is a definition contract assembled from earlier items; well-definedness is discharged by the cited suppliers. (i) The encoding (a) is the real-part-of-complex-amplitude convention of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] with a general $C^\infty$ spatial amplitude; the componentwise real part of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and the complex exponential of [[def-complex-exponential]] are total on $\mathbb C^3$, so the associated real fields are defined for every $C^\infty$ pair, with no equation assumed. (ii) The class (b) is cut out by four equations on the open set $D$: the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] act componentwise on the $C^\infty$ complex fields, and the two constants satisfy $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=c^{-2}$ by [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the displayed third and fourth equations use only complex scalar multiplication, so the class is well-defined without any choice principle. (iii) The physical reading of the associated real fields as an electric and a magnetic field uses [[def-em-fields]]; the units of $\widetilde E$ are V$\,$m$^{-1}$ and those of $\widetilde B$ are T, inherited from that definition. (iv) Clause (c) records exactly what is not asserted; in particular the complex Maxwell-to-real-Maxwell deduction is deliberately left to a consumer, because a definition must not assert the field equations of its associated real fields.

items.title: Real parts of $e^{-i\omega t}$ phasors: calculus, injectivity and equivalence with the real Helmholtz-Maxwell system
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the vector PEC scattering theorem (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $c>0$ and $\omega>0$, and let $\widetilde E,\widetilde B:D\to\mathbb C^3$. Define $E,B:D\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ by $E(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and $B(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde B(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ componentwise ([[def-complex-exponential]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]; [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] for the classes). Then: (a) [Calculus] if $\widetilde E,\widetilde B$ are $C^1$, then $E,B$ are $C^1$ and at every $(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R$: $\partial_tE(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and likewise for $B$; for each $j\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\partial_jE(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\partial_j\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and likewise for $B$; and with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] acting on the spatial variable, $\operatorname{div}E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{div}\widetilde E)(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, $\operatorname{curl}E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E)(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and likewise for $B$. (b) [Injectivity] if $w\in\mathbb C^3$ and $\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})=0$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$, then $w=0$; more generally, if $w:D\to\mathbb C^3$ is continuous and $\operatorname{Re}(w(x)e^{-i\omega t})=0$ for all $(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R$, then $w\equiv0$ on $D$. (c) [Equivalence] if $\widetilde E,\widetilde B$ are $C^1$, the phasor system $$\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=0,\quad\operatorname{div}\widetilde B=0,\quad\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B,\quad\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E$$ holds on $D$ if and only if the real system $$\operatorname{div}E=0,\quad\operatorname{div}B=0,\quad\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\quad\operatorname{curl}B=c^{-2}\partial_tE$$ holds on $D\times\mathbb R$.
items.strategy: Write the encoding in real components: by the Cartesian form and Euler identity of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], $\operatorname{Re}(w(x)e^{-i\omega t})=(\operatorname{Re}w(x))\cos(\omega t)+(\operatorname{Im}w(x))\sin(\omega t)$ componentwise, with the real and imaginary parts of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and the complex arithmetic of [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. (a) For fixed $x$ each component is a constant-coefficient combination of $\cos(\omega t)$ and $\sin(\omega t)$; the sum, scalar-multiple and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] with the derivatives of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] give $\partial_tE=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega\widetilde Ee^{-i\omega t})$, and the spatial derivatives pass through the constant coefficients, giving the spatial formulas for each component; the divergence and curl formulas follow by applying the componentwise formulas and the linearity of [[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]] (for complex fields, componentwise in real and imaginary parts). (b) Evaluating at $t=0$ gives $\operatorname{Re}w=0$; evaluating at $t=\pi/(2\omega)$ gives $\operatorname{Re}(-iw)=\operatorname{Im}w=0$ by the quarter-turn values of [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]] and the Cartesian form of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], so $w=0$. The continuous case applies the pointwise result at each $x\in D$; no choice principle is used. (c) Direction (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii): substitute the phasor equations into the calculus formulas of (a); e.g. $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E)e^{-i\omega t})=\operatorname{Re}(i\omega\widetilde Be^{-i\omega t})=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde Ee^{-i\omega t})=c^{-2}\partial_tE$. Direction (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i): subtract the complex expressions and apply (b), e.g. $\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E-i\omega\widetilde B)e^{-i\omega t})=0$ for all $(x,t)$ forces $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B$; the other three equations are analogous. All statements are pointwise algebraic identities; no PDE existence, no boundary condition and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Periodic responses of $\ddot z=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ and the affine classification of all solutions
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the weak-field Thomson item (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $T:=2\pi/\omega$, $n\ge1$ and $w\in\mathbb C^n$; use the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]]. Define $z_p:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ by $z_p(t):=\operatorname{Re}(-w\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})$ componentwise ([[def-derivative]] for the derivative below). Then: (a) $z_p$ is $C^\infty$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) and satisfies $z_p''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$; it is $T$-periodic. (b) every $C^2$ solution $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ of $z''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ on $\mathbb R$ has the form $z(t)=z_p(t)+a+bt$ with unique $a,b\in\mathbb R^n$. (c) such a solution is $T$-periodic if and only if $b=0$; the $T$-periodic solutions are exactly $z_p(t)+a$, $a\in\mathbb R^n$, and their oscillating part has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$.
items.strategy: (a) By the Cartesian form and Euler identity of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], $z_p(t)=-\omega^{-2}[(\operatorname{Re}w)\cos(\omega t)+(\operatorname{Im}w)\sin(\omega t)]$ componentwise. Differentiating twice with the sum, scalar-multiple and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and the derivatives of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] gives $z_p''=\operatorname{Re}w\cos(\omega t)+\operatorname{Im}w\sin(\omega t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$. Periodicity of $z_p$ follows from $e^{-i\omega(t+T)}=e^{-i\omega t}e^{-i\omega T}=e^{-i\omega t}$ by the addition law of [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]] and $e^{-2\pi i}=1$, the latter from the Cartesian form and the values $\cos2\pi=1$, $\sin2\pi=0$ of [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]]. (b) If $z$ is any $C^2$ solution, then $h:=z-z_p$ satisfies $h''=0$ on $\mathbb R$. Apply [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] on the interval $\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) to each component of $h'$: $h'=b$ is constant. Applying the same corollary to $h-b\,\mathrm{id}$ gives $h=z_p+a+bt$. Uniqueness of $a,b$ from $z(0)$ and $z'(0)$ is immediate. (c) If $b=0$ then $z=z_p+a$ is $T$-periodic by (a). Conversely, if $z$ is $T$-periodic then $z(t+T)-z(t)=bT$ for all $t$, hence $b=0$; then $z-z_p=a$ is the constant part whose complex amplitude is zero, while the oscillating part $z_p$ has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$ by construction. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary model definition for the dipole scattering and Thomson items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $k:=\omega/c$ with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]], $\mu_0>0$ the vacuum permeability of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$ (the complex dipole-moment amplitude, in $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m$). Define, on the punctured space $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ and all times $t\in\mathbb R$, $$E_{\rm d}(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(-\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}\,n\times(n\times p_0)\,e^{i(kr-\omega t)}\Bigr),\qquad B_{\rm d}(x,t):=\frac1c\,n\times E_{\rm d}(x,t),$$ where $r:=|x|$ and $n:=x/r$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), with the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]] and the real-field encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]]. Call $(E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d})$ the **ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of frequency $\omega$ and amplitude $p_0$**, and call $S_{\rm d}:=E_{\rm d}\times B_{\rm d}/\mu_0$ its model flux ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]); the model fields are read as an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]]. [Adopted status] This is an explicitly adopted ideal radiation-law model, fixed by the following declarations: (i) it is the leading transverse far-zone field of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) evaluated at the harmonic transverse moment $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$, i.e. at $p''$ for the waveform $p(u)=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u})$; (ii) the model contains no independent magnetic-dipole or higher-multipole radiation, no near-zone or static field and no other radiating component; (iii) it is not asserted to solve the vacuum Maxwell equations at finite $r$, to be the field of any actual source, to satisfy any boundary condition or to have finite total energy on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$; (iv) for compact smooth conserved sources the difference from the actual retarded fields is controlled only by the explicit absolute bounds of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]]. No measured, empirical or material-response content is adopted: $p_0$ is prescribed model data, not a derived polarizability.
items.strategy: This is a definition contract; well-definedness is discharged by the cited suppliers. (i) The formula is the leading transverse term $E_{\rm lead}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$ of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) at $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$: since $p''(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$ for $p(u)=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u})$, the complex derivative being the one of [[def-complex-exponential]], the model field is exactly $E_{\rm lead}$ rewritten with $u=t-r/c$ and $e^{i(kr-\omega t)}=e^{-i\omega(t-r/c)}$; the cross product, inner product and norm are those of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] and [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. (ii) $r>0$ on the declared domain, so $E_{\rm d}$ and $B_{\rm d}$ are $C^\infty$ there and the real-part encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] applies; $E_{\rm d}\cdot n=0$ because $n\times(n\times p_0)$ is orthogonal to $n$, and $B_{\rm d}=n\times E_{\rm d}/c$ by definition. (iii) The model flux $S_{\rm d}$ is the quantity of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] evaluated at the model fields; that definition applies to any pair of fields of the declared regularity and assigns no field equation. (iv) The status clause lists the model assumptions (i)-(iv) and excludes exact Maxwell, source-realization, boundary, finite-energy and empirical claims; the model's relation to actual sources is only through the explicit bounds of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], which are quantified in the item below. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Adopted scalar aperture-diffraction model (polarization-insensitive regime)
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] and [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] ([[def-countable-choice]]); the smooth modal full-Choice branch of the latter is not used. Adopt as a model assumption of the framework the following scalar aperture-diffraction model. [Data] Fix an angular frequency $\omega>0$ and wavenumber $k:=\omega/c$, with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $S\subset\{y\in\mathbb R^3:y_3=0\}\cap B_a(0)$ be a nonempty compact subset of a declared aperture plane $y_3=0$ with aperture radius $a>0$ (the screening plane and spatial region are read in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]), and let $\alpha$ be a finite complex measure on $\mathbb R^3$ supported in $S$ (the **aperture distribution**), with $\alpha$ read in volts so that the model field below carries the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ of an electric-field component and its pairings are those of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. [Model field] The model assigns to every observation point $x$ with $x_3>0$ the complex scalar amplitude $$u(x):=\int G_k(x-y)\,d\alpha(y),$$ where $G_k(z)=e^{ik|z|}/(4\pi|z|)$ for $z\ne0$ is the outgoing Helmholtz kernel of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], together with the real scalar field $U(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and the model period-averaged squared field $(1/2)|u(x)|^2$. All model predictions are declared comparisons of this squared field between observation points; no absolute radiometric power or intensity calibration is adopted. [Adopted regime and status] The model is the declared polarization-insensitive scalar approximation of aperture diffraction. It ignores the vector nature and polarization of the electromagnetic field, takes the aperture distribution rather than the exact screen traces as its datum, assigns no back-reaction of the diffracted field on the illumination and no screen interaction beyond the aperture, and is not derived from either branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] or from the material-closure branches of [[post-em-material-closure]]; it is a declared optical approximation, not an exact electromagnetic model. It does not assert that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations exactly, and it does not identify $\alpha$ with the unknown exact Maxwell boundary traces: assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently is not a well-posed exact boundary problem, as recorded in [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]], and the error terms of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] are the controlled content of the model. No measured intensity, apparatus, sampling model, uncertainty budget, empirical comparison or quantitative radiometric calibration is adopted.
items.strategy: This is an explicit adopted-assumption contract; it is deliberately not a derivation. (i) The mathematical object it adopts is the outgoing source field $u=G_k*\alpha$ of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], whose kernel, support class and outgoing/Fraunhofer error terms are fixed there; the integral against the finite complex measure is that of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. (ii) The physical reading uses the aperture plane and spatial region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], the wavenumber-frequency relation $k=\omega/c$ and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (iii) The non-derivation clause is essential: neither the smooth nor the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] implies this scalar source model, and the finite-conductivity/material branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] contain no ideal aperture or screen model; the trace caveat is the one recorded in [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]]. (iv) The scope sentences exclude exact Maxwell, vector, polarization, back-reaction, absolute-radiometric and empirical content. The item uses no choice principle beyond those carried by the cited mathematical suppliers (the kernel lemma carries Countable Choice, as stated there). The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited verbatim from the cited kernel and boundary-representation suppliers; this postulate adds no choice use of its own.

items.title: Controlled scalar aperture diffraction: Fresnel and Fraunhofer approximations with explicit error terms
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] and [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] ([[def-countable-choice]]), whose trace qualification is used in clause (d); the full-Choice modal branch of the latter is not used. Adopt the scalar aperture model and its notation from [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]]: frequency $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, aperture radius $a>0$, finite complex aperture distribution $\alpha$ supported in the planar aperture $S\subset\{y_3=0\}\cap B_a(0)$, model field $u=G_k*\alpha$, real field $U(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and $T=2\pi/\omega$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-complex-exponential]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]). Set $I(x):=(1/2)|u(x)|^2$. Then: (a) [Model field and Fraunhofer estimate] $u$ is $C^\infty$ on the half-space $\{x_3>0\}$ and on $\mathbb R^3\setminus S$, satisfies $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ there, and is outgoing in the sense of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]]: for $x=rn$ with $r\ge2a$ and $n\in S^2$, $$u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)+O\Bigl(\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}}{r}\Bigl[\frac ar+\frac{ka^2}{r}\Bigr]\Bigr)$$ uniformly in direction, and $r(\partial_ru-iku)=O(r^{-1})$ uniformly. (b) [Fresnel estimate] for the planar aperture and observation $x=(\xi_1,\xi_2,z)$ with $z>0$, $|\xi|\le b$ and $a+b\ll z$, the Fresnel approximation replaces $R=|x-y|$ by $z+|\xi-y|^2/(2z)$ and $1/R$ by $1/z$ in the model integral with phase error $O(k(a+b)^4/z^3)$, relative amplitude error $O((a+b)^2/z^2)$ and absolute field error $O(\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}z^{-1}[(a+b)^2/z^2+k(a+b)^4/z^3])$. (c) [Intensity and error transfer] at every $x$ with $x_3>0$ the model period average satisfies $\frac1T\int_0^TU(x,s)^2\,ds=I(x)$ ([[lem-em-period-average]]). If $u_{\rm approx}$ is any approximation of $u$ with $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\delta(x)$, then $|\frac12|u_{\rm approx}(x)|^2-I(x)|\le\frac12\delta(x)(|u(x)|+|u_{\rm approx}(x)|)$; if moreover $u(x)\ne0$ and $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\epsilon(x)|u(x)|$, the relative intensity error is at most $2\epsilon(x)+\epsilon(x)^2$. In particular the Fraunhofer and Fresnel field errors of (a) and (b) bound the corresponding intensity errors; no new approximation is introduced by passing to $I$. (d) [Trace and scope] the aperture distribution $\alpha$ is an adopted model datum and is not identified with the exact Maxwell boundary data on the screen; assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently does not produce a well-posed exact boundary problem ([[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]]). The construction ignores polarization and aperture back-reaction, makes no claim that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations exactly, and makes no measured-intensity, apparatus, sampling or empirical claim; only comparisons of $I$ between observation points are read as model predictions.
items.strategy: The theorem instantiates the mathematical field estimates of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] at the adopted model datum of [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]]. (a) is exactly the supplier's statement for $u=G_k*\alpha$ with $\alpha$ supported in $B_a(0)$ intersected with the aperture plane, including the uniform Fraunhofer error, the outgoing residual and the off-support smoothness; no re-derivation is needed because the model field is defined to be that supplier's field. (b) is the supplier's planar-aperture Fresnel estimate, whose phase and amplitude errors are Taylor-remainder bounds for $R=|x-y|$ on the compact small-$s$ region $s=|\xi-y|^2/z^2$; the same estimates apply to the model because the datum is the same finite complex measure. (c) applies [[lem-em-period-average]] with $a=d=u(x)$: $\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})^2$ averages to $\frac12\operatorname{Re}(u(x)\overline{u(x)})=\frac12|u(x)|^2$. The first error bound is the identity $\frac12||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2|=\frac12|u_{\rm approx}-u|\,||u_{\rm approx}|+|u||$ together with $||u_{\rm approx}|-|u||\le|u_{\rm approx}-u|$; the relative bound is $||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2|/|u|^2\le\epsilon(2+\epsilon)$. No choice principle beyond that carried by the suppliers is used. (d) reproduces the trace distinction of [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] and the model-scope declarations of the postulate; the intensity reading is the declared one, so no radiometric claim is added. The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited from the cited suppliers; the intensity computation of (c) uses only the choice-free period-average lemma.

items.title: Monochromatic scattering by a smooth perfect-electric-conductor obstacle
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as carried by [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]], whose variational, Sobolev-compactness and compact-spectral steps use it; the algebraic computations below use no further choice. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary, $D:=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ connected, $k>0$, $\omega:=ck$ with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$; let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open with $\overline D\subseteq V$, and let $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})$ be a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on $V$ ([[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Plane-wave instances are provided by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]]: if $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$ and $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, then $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})(x)=(e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x},b\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x})$ satisfies the four phasor equations on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]). Adopt the ideal perfectly conducting (PEC) boundary model: the tangential component of the total electric field vanishes on $\partial O$. This is a declared idealization of the stationary interface conditions of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] with vanishing fields inside the conductor; it is not one of the finite-conductivity branches of [[post-em-material-closure]], and the induced surface charge and current are neither prescribed nor determined here. Let $e_T$ be the tangential projection of $-\widetilde E_{\rm inc}$ on $\partial O$, and let $\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ be the unique $C^\infty$ field on $\overline D$ of [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] with $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ on $D$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$ and that lemma's outgoing modal condition on $S_R$. Set $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}:=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ and, on $D$, $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}:=\widetilde E_{\rm inc}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$, $\widetilde B_{\rm tot}:=\widetilde B_{\rm inc}+\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$. Then: (a) [Phasor Maxwell] $(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ and $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ are $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pairs on $D$; and for every $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair $(\widetilde E,\widetilde B)$ on an open set $O'\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, the associated real fields of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]] satisfy on $O'\times\mathbb R$ the smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho\equiv0$ and $J\equiv0$. Consequently the associated real total fields $E_{\rm tot},B_{\rm tot}$ satisfy those source-free equations on $D\times\mathbb R$. (b) [PEC boundary condition] the tangential trace of $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}$ on $\partial O$ vanishes; hence for every unit normal field $n$ of $\partial O$ the associated real total electric field $E_{\rm tot}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E_{\rm tot}(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) satisfies $n\times E_{\rm tot}=0$ on $\partial O\times\mathbb R$. (c) [Uniqueness] if $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')$ is a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on an open set $V'\supseteq\overline D$ that is outgoing on $S_R$ in the modal sense of the vector Helmholtz lemma and has tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$, then $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')=(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ on $D$; equivalently $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ is the unique outgoing total pair with the prescribed incident phasor and $n\times E_{\rm tot}=0$ on $\partial O$. (d) [Scope] one positive frequency $\omega=ck$, one smooth bounded stationary PEC obstacle with connected exterior, and $C^\infty$ incident and scattered classes only; no lossy, impedance, nonsmooth or dispersive obstacle, no determination of the induced surface charge or current, no radiation-zone amplitude or far-field asymptotics beyond the lemma's outgoing modal class, no point or singular source, no finite-energy or empirical claim.
items.strategy: Assume the Axiom of Choice exactly through [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] (its symmetry/coercivity, compactness and compact-spectral steps); all other steps are pointwise algebra. (a) For the scattered pair: $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ is the boundary-problem condition; $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=i\omega\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ holds by the definition of $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$; $\operatorname{div}\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}(\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=(i\omega)^{-1}(\nabla\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}-\Delta\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=(i\omega)^{-1}k^2\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ by [[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]], [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$; the sum of two solutions of the linear system is a solution by [[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]. The real-field Maxwell statement is clause (c) of [[lem-em-phasor-real-part-calculus-and-equivalence]] with the constant $c$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]], combined with the identification of its real system with the zero-source smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the incident pair is a pair on $V$, hence on $D$. (b) The tangential traces satisfy $\widetilde E_{\rm tot,tang}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat,tang}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+e_T=0$ on $\partial O$; the associated real field is the real part of the tangential trace, hence vanishes (the encoding and real-part calculus are those of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]] and [[lem-em-phasor-real-part-calculus-and-equivalence]]). (c) A candidate $\widetilde E'$ of the stated class satisfies all hypotheses of the uniqueness assertion of [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] for the same tangential data, so $\widetilde E'=\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$; then $\widetilde B'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ by the third phasor equation of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]]. (d) records the exact scope; in particular the ideal PEC condition is adopted, not derived, and the material-closure branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] contain no $\sigma\to\infty$ branch, while [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] supplies only the stationary-interface idealization context.

items.title: Differential and total cross sections of the ideal harmonic dipole in a plane-wave field
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] and [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] ([[def-countable-choice]]); the period-average and cross-section algebra itself uses no choice. Adopt the ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of [[def-em-ideal-harmonic-dipole-model]] with frequency $\omega>0$, wavenumber $k=\omega/c$ and amplitude $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$; let $E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d},S_{\rm d}$ be its fields and model flux. Let $\kappa\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, $e\in\mathbb C^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b:=\kappa\times e/\omega$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and let $(E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc})$ be the corresponding plane-wave fields of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$; by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] they satisfy the smooth-branch source-free vacuum Maxwell equations, and by [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]](b) their period-averaged energy flux has magnitude $I_{\rm inc}=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2=\frac{|e|^2}{2\mu_0c}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). Define the **model differential scattering cross section** by $$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n):=\frac{r^2\langle S_{\rm d}(rn,\cdot)\cdot n\rangle}{\langle S_{\rm inc}\cdot\hat\kappa\rangle},\qquad n\in S^2,\ r>0,$$ where $\hat\kappa:=\kappa/|\kappa|$, $S_{\rm inc}:=E_{\rm inc}\times B_{\rm inc}/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]), and $\langle f\rangle:=\frac1T\int_0^Tf(s)\,ds$, $T=2\pi/\omega$, is the period average at fixed observation point. Then: (a) [Angular pattern] the ratio is independent of $r$ and of the averaging start, and for every $n\in S^2$ $$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2|e|^2}.$$ (b) [Total cross section] with $d\sigma_{S^2}$ the surface measure of the unit sphere, $\sigma:=\int_{S^2}\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}\,d\sigma_{S^2}$ equals $$\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2};$$ if $p_0=\alpha e$ for a complex scalar $\alpha$ (the scalar polarizability, in $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^2$), then $\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$ and $\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4}|n\times\hat e|^2$ with $\hat e:=e/|e|$. (c) [Fidelity to the compact-source dipole theorem] the model field is exactly the leading transverse field $E_{\rm lead}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$ of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) evaluated at the harmonic transverse moment $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$. Consequently, for an actual source of that theorem's class, the difference between its retarded field at $(rn,u+r/c)$ and the model field is bounded by $\Gamma_E/r^2+\mu_0D(u)/(2\pi r)$ in the electric field and by $(\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c)/r^2$ plus $c^{-1}$ times that bound in the magnetic field, uniformly in $n$, where $D(u)$ is that theorem's explicit source-variation bound ([[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](b)-(c)); no smallness of $D(u)$ is asserted. (d) [Scope] conditional predictions of the adopted ideal model: no measured cross section, no frequency-domain response law (the amplitude $p_0$ is prescribed model data), no magnetic-dipole or higher-multipole content, no self-force, material response, finite-size or empirical claim; the scalar-$\alpha$ clause records a declared proportional response, not a derived polarizability.
items.strategy: (a) In the model, $B_{\rm d}=n\times E_{\rm d}/c$ and $n\cdot E_{\rm d}=0$, so $S_{\rm d}\cdot n=n\cdot(E_{\rm d}\times(n\times E_{\rm d}))/(\mu_0c)=|E_{\rm d}|^2/(\mu_0c)$ pointwise; writing $w:=\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p_0)e^{ikr}$, the model has $E_{\rm d}=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$, and [[lem-em-period-average]] gives $\langle|E_{\rm d}|^2\rangle=\frac12|w|^2=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4}{32\pi^2r^2}|n\times p_0|^2$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). Hence $r^2\langle S_{\rm d}\cdot n\rangle=\frac{\mu_0\omega^4}{32\pi^2c}|n\times p_0|^2$, independent of $r$ and of the averaging start. Division by the incident flux $I_{\rm inc}=\frac{|e|^2}{2\mu_0c}$ of [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]](b) and $\mu_0^2=\frac1{\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]) give the two displayed forms. (b) [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d) gives $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=\frac{8\pi}3|a|^2$ for real $a$, and applying it to the real and imaginary parts of $p_0$ gives the complex case; integrating the pattern of (a) over $S^2$ yields $\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4}{16\pi^2|e|^2}\cdot\frac{8\pi}3|p_0|^2=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2}$, i.e. the two displayed forms. For $p_0=\alpha e$ substitute $|p_0|^2=|\alpha|^2|e|^2$ and $|n\times p_0|^2=|\alpha|^2|e|^2|n\times\hat e|^2$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). (c) With $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$, the model field is $E_{\rm lead}$ of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) at $(rn,t)$ with $u=t-r/c$; that theorem's clause (b) bounds the difference between the actual transverse moment $V_{\rm act}$ and $p''$, and its clause (c) bounds the actual field against $E_{\rm lead}(V_{\rm act})$ by $\Gamma_E/r^2+\mu_0D(u)/(4\pi r)$ and the magnetic remainder by $(\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c)/r^2$; inserting the triangle inequality and $|n\times(n\times p'')-n\times(n\times V_{\rm act})|\le|V_{\rm act}-p''|$ gives the displayed electric bound, while the magnetic bound follows by adding $c^{-1}$ times the field difference via the cross-product norm estimate of [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]. (d) records the scope; no measured or material content is added ([[def-em-si-conventions]] only fixes units and constants). No choice principle beyond that carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] and [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] (Countable Choice, as stated there) is used. The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited from the cited period-average and sphere-moment suppliers; the algebra and period averages add no choice use.

items.title: Controlled first variation of the relativistic test-charge law: the leading Thomson-model cross section
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]]; the linearization below and [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]] use no choice. Assume the setting and postulates of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] for a test particle with charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-sources]](a)) and externally supplied rest mass $m>0$, in the incident plane-wave field of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with wavevector $\kappa$, complex amplitude $e\ne0$, $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $|\kappa|=\omega/c$ and $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$ as in [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]]; write $E_{\rm inc}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(\kappa\cdot x-\omega t)})$ and $B_{\rm inc}=\kappa\times E_{\rm inc}/\omega$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Assume that for some $\eta_0>0$ and a common open interval $I\ni0$, for every $\eta\in(-\eta_0,\eta_0)$ there is a $C^2$ future timelike massive solution $r_\eta:I\to\mathbb R^3$ of the adopted four-force law in the external field $\eta(E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc})$ (no self-field, recoil or material force), and that the family admits a uniform first-order expansion: there are $r_1\in C^2(I;\mathbb R^3)$ and, for every compact $K\subset I$, a constant $C_K$ with $$|r_\eta(t)-x_0-\eta r_1(t)|+|\dot r_\eta(t)-\eta\dot r_1(t)|\le C_K\eta^2\qquad(t\in K,\ |\eta|\le\eta_0)$$ about a fixed position $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, and the first-order displacement $z_1:=r_1$ is $T$-periodic, $T=2\pi/\omega$. Then: (a) [Linearized equation] $\ddot r_1(t)=\frac qmE_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)=\frac qm\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(\kappa\cdot x_0-\omega t)})$ on $I$. (b) [Induced dipole] with $x_0$ the particle's mean position, the oscillating part of the first-order dipole moment $q(r_1-z_1^{\rm mean})$ is $\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega t})$ with complex amplitude $$p_0=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}\,e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0};$$ equivalently $p_0=\alpha e'$ with $\alpha=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}$ (units $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^2$) and the unimodular factor $e'=e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$, $|e'|=|e|$. (c) [Leading Thomson-model cross section] substituting this $p_0$ into [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]](b) gives $$\sigma_{\rm T}=\frac{q^4}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}=\frac{8\pi}{3}\Bigl(\frac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0mc^2}\Bigr)^2,$$ independent of $\omega$ and of the phase factor. (d) [Scope] this is a controlled conditional first variation of the adopted relativistic external-force law under the stated solution-family hypotheses. It is not the exact Newtonian force postulate, it does not assert existence, persistence, stability or self-consistency of the family, it excludes self-force, radiation reaction and material media, and it makes no empirical, measurement, atomic-physics or frequency-response claim.
items.strategy: The proof is the $\eta\to0$ linearization of the coordinate form of the adopted four-force law, followed by the periodic-response lemma and the substitution into the cross-section theorem. (i) Along the family, [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]](a) gives $m\frac{d}{dt}(\gamma_\eta\dot r_\eta)=q\eta(E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta,t)+\dot r_\eta\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta,t))$. By the expansion, $|\dot r_\eta|=O(\eta)$ uniformly on each compact $K$, so clause (c) of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] with fixed $\delta$ gives $\gamma_\eta=1+O(\eta^2)$. Hence $m\frac{d}{dt}(\gamma_\eta\dot r_\eta)=m\ddot r_\eta+O(\eta^2)=m\eta\ddot r_1+O(\eta^2)$; the magnetic term is $q\eta\dot r_\eta\times B_{\rm inc}=O(\eta^2)$; and the electric term is $q\eta E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta,t)=q\eta E_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)+O(\eta^2)$ because $E_{\rm inc}$ is smooth and $r_\eta-x_0=O(\eta)$ uniformly on $K$. Dividing by $\eta$ and letting $\eta\to0$ gives (a). (ii) By (a) and [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]](b)-(c) with $w=\frac qme e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$, the $T$-periodic $r_1$ equals $\operatorname{Re}(-\frac q{m\omega^2}e e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}e^{-i\omega t})+a$; subtracting its mean $a$, the oscillating displacement has complex amplitude $-\frac q{m\omega^2}e e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$, so the oscillating dipole moment $q(r_1-a)$ has amplitude $p_0=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}e e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$; the phase factor is unimodular, so $|p_0|=\frac{q^2|e|}{m\omega^2}$ and $p_0=\alpha e'$ with $\alpha=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}$, $|e'|=|e|$. (iii) Inserting $p_0=\alpha e'$ into [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]](b) gives $\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4}=\frac{q^4}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}$, and the parenthesis is $\frac{8\pi}3r_q^2$ with $r_q=\frac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0mc^2}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]] for the constants). (iv) No choice principle is used here: the linearization is finite-dimensional calculus, the periodic-response lemma is choice-free, and the cross-section substitution is algebra; the Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited from the cross-section theorem being substituted into.

items.title: Uniform rectangular aperture: the Fraunhofer sinc-squared pattern
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]] and by the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison and Fubini suppliers used in the integral reduction below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the scalar aperture model of [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]] and [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]], with frequency $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, aperture plane $y_3=0$, model field $u=G_k*\alpha$ and $I(x)=\frac12|u(x)|^2$. Fix $a>0$, $b>0$ and $A_0\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$; identify the rectangle $R:=[-a,a]\times[-b,b]\subset\mathbb R^2$ with the planar aperture $\{(y_1,y_2,0):(y_1,y_2)\in R\}$ and take the **uniform rectangular aperture distribution** $$\alpha:=A_0\,\lambda_R,\qquad \alpha(E):=A_0\,\lambda_2(E\cap R)\ \text{ for Borel } E\subseteq\mathbb R^2,$$ the finite complex measure of constant density $A_0$ on $R$ with respect to the two-dimensional Lebesgue measure $\lambda_2$ ([[def-multidimensional-rectangle-and-volume]], [[def-measure-with-density]], [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]). Then: (a) [Fraunhofer amplitude] with $\operatorname{sinc}\xi:=\sin\xi/\xi$ for $\xi\ne0$ and $\operatorname{sinc}0:=1$, the Fraunhofer amplitude factor of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a) is exactly $$\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)=4abA_0\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)\qquad(n=(n_1,n_2,n_3)\in S^2),$$ an identity for every direction $n$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-complex-exponential]], [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]], [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]). (b) [Fraunhofer intensity] in the Fraunhofer regime of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a) with aperture radius $a':=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, i.e. for $r\ge2a'$, the model intensity is $$I_{\rm F}(rn)=\frac{a^2b^2|A_0|^2}{2\pi^2r^2}\operatorname{sinc}^2(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}^2(kb\,n_2)$$ up to the Fraunhofer absolute error of that theorem, transferred to $I$ by its clause (c). The pattern vanishes exactly where $ka\,n_1\in\pi\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ or $kb\,n_2\in\pi\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, and has its central maximum at $n=(0,0,\pm1)$. (c) [Scope] this is an exact computation inside the adopted ideal scalar model, not a measured diffraction record: no absolute radiometric calibration, polarization content, screen interaction, apparatus model or sampling law is asserted, and the Fraunhofer/Fresnel error bounds of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]] are inherited rather than re-estimated.
items.strategy: (a) Because $\alpha=A_0\lambda_R$ has density $A_0$ with respect to $\lambda_2$ on $R$, [[def-measure-with-density]] and [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]] give $\int f\,d\alpha=A_0\int_Rf\,d\lambda_2$ for every bounded Borel $f$ (apply the identity to the positive density $|A_0|$ and multiply by the unimodular factor $A_0/|A_0|$, with real and imaginary parts by [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]). For $f(y)=e^{-ik(n_1y_1+n_2y_2)}$ (the $y_3$-coordinate is zero on the aperture, and $n\cdot y=n_1y_1+n_2y_2$ by [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), $f$ is continuous on the compact rectangle $R$ ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]), so [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies the Lebesgue integral with the Riemann double integral; [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] factors it into the product of the two one-dimensional integrals. For $\xi\ne0$, the one-dimensional integral is $\int_{-a}^aI_0\,e^{-ikn_1y_1}\,dy_1=2\sin(ka\,n_1)/(kn_1)=2a\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)$ by [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] applied to the real and imaginary parts via [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]; for $n_1=0$ it equals $2a=2a\operatorname{sinc}0$ by the defining limit value, so the formula holds for every direction. The second factor is analogous, giving the displayed product $4abA_0\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)$. (b) Insert the product amplitude into the Fraunhofer expression $u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}d\alpha(y)+$error of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a), square the modulus and use $I=\frac12|u|^2$; the modulus of the amplitude is $4ab|A_0||\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)||\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)|$, so $|u_{\rm F}|^2=\frac{a^2b^2|A_0|^2}{\pi^2r^2}\operatorname{sinc}^2(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}^2(kb\,n_2)$ and the factor $\frac12$ gives the displayed $I_{\rm F}$. The vanishing/central-maximum reading is the elementary zero set of $\xi\mapsto\sin\xi/\xi$: $\operatorname{sinc}\xi=0$ exactly for $\xi\in\pi\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, and $|\operatorname{sinc}\xi|\le1$ with equality at $\xi=0$ away from those zeros. The support of $\alpha$ lies in $B_{a'}(0)$ with $a'=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, so the theorem's Fraunhofer condition $r\ge2a$ is met at $r\ge2a'$; clause (c) of the theorem transfers the field error to $I$. (c) is the scope of the model; no additional approximation is introduced. The computation uses only the standard Riemann/Lebesgue and trigonometric suppliers listed in the dependencies; the Countable Choice assumption is exactly the one carried by the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison and Fubini interfaces, with no additional choice.
